answer: The surveyor's chain rattles across the heath, and the cartographer inks the coastline by lamplight. Proof of cartographer map via survey chain log — a chain the cartographer stretches only after 19 chains run true, each chain surveyed by the cartographer himself. The velvet is the hill the chain is stretched from. The vault is the compass the bearings are taken with. The beacon is the sheet the finished chart is drawn on. Matching the survey needs 19 steady hands on the chain, and the forger brings only two.
